title: LearnGraph: A Learning-Based Architecture for Dynamic Graph Processing
problem: Dynamic graph processing systems using conventional array-based architectures suffer from inefficient memory access patterns and poor index management, limiting throughput.
method: Proposes an adaptive tree-based memory manager with two components: (1) hierarchical learned index optimized for graph topology to predict vertex and edge locations, and (2) adaptive tree structure that dynamically reorganizes memory regions based on access patterns.

title: Design and Operation of Shared Machine Learning Clusters on Campus
problem: Academic GPU clusters must be shared equitably among many users with diverse ML workloads, but existing cluster management solutions are designed for large industrial settings and do not address the operational challenges specific to campus environments: limited staffing, heterogeneous hardware, fair multi-user resource allocation, and incident management at small scale.
method: SING provides a four-layer extensible architecture for shared GPU cluster management: a hardware/infrastructure layer (automated configuration and monitoring), a resource scheduling layer (fair allocation policies across users and jobs), an interface layer (user-facing job submission and access controls), and an operations layer (incident detection, logging, and management). The system is designed to minimize maintenance costs with limited staffing by automating routine operations, and to optimize utilization through workload-aware scheduling policies.

title: Pruner: A Draft-then-Verify Exploration Mechanism to Accelerate Tensor Program Tuning
problem: Search-based tensor program tuning for deep neural network deployment is slow because the exploration mechanism applies an accurate-but-slow learned cost model to all candidate schedules, taking hours or days to find optimal programs. Additionally, learned cost models trained on one hardware platform cannot adapt online to a new platform, causing performance degradation in cross-platform deployment scenarios.
method: Pruner introduces a 'Draft-then-Verify' exploration mechanism: a fast Symbol-based Analyzer (draft model) rapidly screens a large pool of schedule candidates using lightweight symbolic analysis, producing a small set of promising drafts. The expensive learned cost model then verifies only these filtered candidates. MoA-Pruner extends this with a Momentum online Adaptation strategy that uses momentum-based gradient updates to adapt the cost model incrementally to new hardware platforms during the tuning process itself, addressing cross-platform unawareness without full retraining.

title: M5: Mastering Page Migration and Memory Management for CXL-based Tiered Memory Systems
problem: CXL DRAM has 2-3x higher access latency than DDR DRAM, requiring effective page migration between tiers. Existing CPU-driven page-migration solutions misclassify warm pages as hot pages, fail to handle sparse hot-word pages (where only a small fraction of words in a page are hot), and incur high profiling overhead that can itself degrade application performance.
method: M5 implements a CXL-driven profiling solution that precisely and transparently counts accesses to every 4KB page and 64B cache-line word in CXL DRAM using hardware-based hot-page and hot-word trackers embedded in the CXL controller. Unlike CPU-driven approaches that rely on perf counters or OS page-fault sampling (which conflate warm and hot pages), the CXL controller observes all accesses on the CXL interconnect at cache-line granularity. The hot-page and hot-word trackers enable targeted migration: hot words can be promoted individually (sub-page granularity) for applications with sparse hot pages, avoiding unnecessary full-page migrations.

title: A Systematic Approach for Multi-objective Double-side Clock Tree Synthesis
problem: As semiconductor devices scale, utilizing back-side silicon space via double-side clock trees requires systematic design resource allocation and multi-objective optimization, but existing tools only hack single-side approaches.
method: The approach performs hierarchical clock routing with concurrent buffers and nano Through-Silicon-Via (nTSV) insertion, followed by skew refinement on double-side metal layers. It systematically allocates resources across back- and front-side, jointly optimizing latency, skew, wirelength, and via/buffer count through a unified optimization framework.

title: High-Performance Computing Architecture Exploration with Stage-Enhanced Bayesian Optimization
problem: Automated design space exploration for complex HPC processor architectures faces combinatorial explosion and time-consuming simulation bottlenecks, making it difficult to find power-performance-area efficient designs like Arm Neoverse V1.
method: SEBO (Stage-Enhanced Bayesian Optimization) enhances multi-objective Bayesian optimization by improving three main stages: initial sampling, surrogate model construction, and acquisition function design to intelligently navigate the design space and identify Pareto-optimal Neoverse V1 configurations.

title: DDRoute: a Novel Depth-Driven Approach to the Qubit Routing Problem
problem: Qubit routing compilation in NISQ devices inserts SWAP operations to satisfy topological constraints, but current heuristics produce circuits with incompatible depth overhead for hardware limits.
method: DDRoute uses depth-driven heuristic to solve qubit routing problem (QRP) with explicit optimization for circuit depth. Algorithm prioritizes depth reduction over other routing metrics when inserting SWAP operations.

title: lambda-trim: Optimizing Function Initialization in Serverless Applications With Cost-driven Debloating
problem: In serverless FaaS platforms, Function Initialization (package import, module loading) accounts for more than 50% of the monetary cost of cold starts in real-world ML applications, yet existing optimization efforts focus on the container/VM startup phase rather than the Python initialization phase.
method: lambda-trim uses a three-stage automated pipeline: a static analyzer identifies the reachable module dependency graph for a given serverless function, a profiler specialized for the serverless pricing model (which accounts for both memory usage and wall-clock time as billing dimensions) quantifies the latency and cost contribution of each module, and a debloater removes redundant code paths and unused modules while preserving correctness. The optimized application is directly deployable on standard serverless platforms without runtime changes.

title: MILLION: MasterIng Long-Context LLM Inference Via Outlier-Immunized KV Product QuaNtization
problem: Long-context LLM inference faces two bottlenecks: (1) quadratic attention complexity causing slowdowns as sequence length increases, and (2) KV cache size scaling linearly with context length; traditional quantization fails due to outliers and on-the-fly de-quantization overhead.
method: MILLION applies product quantization to KV cache with non-uniform quantization schemes that handle outliers, implements a high-performance GPU kernel with efficient attention computation and asynchronous quantization pipeline, and leverages sparse computation to minimize on-the-fly quantization/de-quantization overhead.

title: Guarder: A Stable and Lightweight Reconfigurable RRAM-based PIM Accelerator for DNN IP Protection
problem: RRAM-based processing-in-memory accelerators suffer from imprecise weights due to programming stochasticity, limiting model accuracy, and cannot effectively utilize conventional weight encryption/decryption IP protection schemes.
method: Guarder proposes a software-hardware co-design: (1) Hardware: 3T2R cells for reliable MAC operations and reconfigurable inverter operating voltages to encode encryption keys directly in RRAM, (2) Software: Contrastive training ensures high accuracy on authorized chips and degraded performance on unauthorized ones.

title: ADVISOR: Approximate Computing-frienDly High-LeVel Synthesis DesIgn Space ExplORer
problem: High-level synthesis (HLS) enables rapid exploration of hardware implementations, but when combined with approximate computing trade-offs, each design variant must be fully approximated to evaluate area/power vs. accuracy trade-offs, resulting in prohibitively long exploration time.
method: ADVISOR accelerates HLS design space exploration via a static Approximation Friendliness Index (AFI) metric that quickly scores each design for its amenability to approximation. Only designs with high AFI are fully approximated; this filters the design space without expensive full approximation on all variants, achieving 68x speedup over exhaustive exploration.

title: RUPlace: Optimizing Routability via Unified Placement and Routing Formulation
problem: Placement optimization in advanced VLSI designs struggles with routing congestion management; existing methods lack theoretical foundations and decouple placement from routing, missing optimization synergies.
method: ADMM-based placer that alternately optimizes global routing and incremental placement using Wasserstein distance and bilevel optimization. A convex programming model determines optimal cell inflation ratios for global placement while directly minimizing routed congestion.

title: Re4PUF: A Reliable, Reconfigurable ReRAM-based PUF Resilient to DNN and Side Channel Attacks
problem: ReRAM-based Physical Unclonable Functions suffer from unreliability due to read noise and temperature variations, and are vulnerable to Deep Neural Network modeling attacks and Side Channel Attacks.
method: Re4PUF proposes a 3T2R ReRAM-based reconfigurable PUF with digital voltage division cells to improve reliability against read noise and temperature. Adjustable analog inverter supply voltages enable low-cost reconfigurability without ReRAM reprogramming, mitigating DNN and side channel vulnerabilities.

title: A Data-Centric Hardware Accelerator for Efficient Adaptive Radix Tree
problem: Adaptive Radix Tree (ART) operations suffer from redundant tree traversals and high synchronization costs during concurrent read/write operations in databases and key-value stores.
method: Proposes DCART, a data-centric hardware accelerator that exploits temporal and spatial similarities in workloads; coalesces operations targeting the same ART nodes and adaptively caches frequently traversed nodes and their search results.

title: ASDR: Exploiting Adaptive Sampling and Data Reuse for CIM-based Instant Neural Rendering
problem: Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) inference exhibits irregular memory access patterns and high computational overhead, making it unsuitable for low-latency, power-efficient deployment on edge devices. Standard compute architectures cannot bridge the gap between NeRF's memory-bound irregular accesses and the immediacy/power requirements of practical neural rendering.
method: ASDR maps NeRF inference onto computing-in-memory (CIM) arrays to address the memory access bottleneck by performing computation near data storage, eliminating costly DRAM transfers. Adaptive sampling reduces the number of points sampled per ray dynamically based on scene complexity, cutting redundant computation. Data reuse strategies exploit spatial and temporal coherence across adjacent rays and frames to avoid redundant CIM macro activations. Together, these techniques reduce both the number of operations and the energy per operation on the CIM substrate.

title: GoPTX: Fine-grained GPU Kernel Fusion by PTX-level Instruction Flow Weaving
problem: Concurrent kernel execution on GPUs misses opportunities to mitigate warp stalls and improve instruction-level parallelism (ILP) through inter-kernel resource sharing due to sequential default execution of kernels.
method: GoPTX performs fine-grained kernel fusion at the PTX (Parallel Thread Execution) instruction level by establishing a merged control flow graph, interleaving instructions from multiple kernels to minimize pipeline stalls on data hazards; proposes latency-aware instruction weaving algorithm and adaptive code slicing to enlarge scheduling space.
